text:
Viktor Arvidsson hasn't scored in ten games and hasn't had a point in eight. Detroit has lost most of those nights, and one post this week summed up the mood: he and Alex DeBrincat "have gone cold, and with them, the Detroit Red Wings have fallen on hard times."

Our numbers split the slump in two. The goal drought looks like bad luck: 3.0 expected goals (the quality of his chances) in those ten games, and 8 goals on 10.4 expected for the season, so we flag him as due. The point drought is less comforting, because the chances with him on the ice have thinned (9.8 on-ice expected goals against 12.1 usual), and Detroit has scored 4.3 fewer goals than expected with him out there.

At 33, on his fifth NHL team, his game is still the one that made him: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile of forwards for chances from in front of the net last season, and Evolving-Hockey rated him 47th of 401 forwards. Watch whether his line starts generating again; for a player like this, the finishing tends to follow the looks.
